EE ADAS Ultrasonic Mechanical Integration
Introduction
Purpose
Comment00105316
The purpose of this specification is to provide design, packaging and body engineers the mechanical integration and positional requirements for the AAD Level 2+ & Level 3 ultrasonic sensors low speed manuevaring.
Scope
Comment00105317
This standard applies to Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) vehicles which use ultrasonic sensors for Low Speed Manoeuvring (LSM) applications.
Revision History
Comment00105318
[October 2022 / Version 1 / pgote]
Terminology
Acronyms / Abbreviations
Comment00105319
Definitions
Comment00359140
the sensor's 180º Field of View refers to the semisphere centered at the sensor's membrane that would represent the FoV of the sensor if the sensor's FoV was 180º for the Vertical and Horizontal directions.
Requirements
Positional Overview
Comment00110751
The positional overview of Ultrasonic sensors for low speed manoeuvring (LSM) is shown below.
Integration Requirements
Sensor Position
Vehicle Level
Dimensional parameters - vehicle level
The dimensional variation analysis shall be performed for the dimensional parameters of the sensors such as Z position and beta angle with respect to vehicle co-ordinate system.
Beta angle - vehicle level
Vertical angles between the sensor and the ground plane (β-angle) shall be in the range of +/- 3º with respect to nominal value considering vehicle co-ordinate system.
The Z position tolerance - vehicle level
The Z position tolerance of the sensor shall be equal to ± 5 mm with respect to nominal value considering vehicle co-ordinate system
Sensor Level
USS axis system
USS axis system
Dimensional parameters - sensor level

sensor flushness value

Integration of Ultrasonic sensors

The ultrasonic sensor integration shall ensure that the sensor's field of view is clear of obstructions of any part of the bumper's geometry.

Comment00359087
Example of non compliance with Requirement01024789: a surface with a slope of less than 45º impacts the sensor's 180º FoV
Requirement01017189
The supplier shall review the sensor position layout and bumper design provided by JLR and provide assessment on any risks identified.
NOTE: this requirement covers the need to have an early assessment from the supplier, in the role or technical expert, as a sign off for the design phase.
Comment00357237
[RQ_340] For vehicles with same wheelbase and steering geometry, a common sensor layout shall be used in order to maintain the same configuration settings required by the ECU.
Commodity strategy
Where the vehicle program includes variants that introduce modifications affecting the sensor's field of view, the ultrasonic sensor integration shall be agreed with the supplier.
Movable vehicle parts influence on sensor FOV
The ultrasonic sensor integration shall ensure that the sensor's field of view is clear of obstructions by any vehicle moving parts in the entire range of their movement.
Comment00357238
Example of "vehicle moving parts" are: Headlamp cleaners, wheels on the steering axles, doors and deployable side steps (DODS integration), active spoiler, Tailgate.
Vehicle accessories consideration
The ultrasonic sensor integration shall ensure that the sensor's field of view is clear of obstructions from any accessory listed in the accessory vigenette.

chunks.content_text:
Vehicle accessories consideration
The ultrasonic sensor integration shall ensure that the sensor's field of view is clear of obstructions from any accessory listed in the accessory vigenette.
NOTE: This requirement does not apply to accessories used in the event of vehicle breakdown (in particular to towing eyes and towing ropes)
Comment00360122
Example of accesories are: towbar, winch, spare wheel cover, lamp guards, bike carriers.
Requirement01014344
The supplier shall provide asessment for any accesory or moveable part that affects the field of view, delivering a document with final statement and suggested actions.
Integration near openings and cavities
The ultrasonic sensor integration shall ensure that the sensor's 180º FoV has a clearance of minimum 3mm, in addition to the build tolerances, from any openings or cavities of the bumper. NOTE: Any deviation to this requirement shall be agreed by the supplier.
Requirement01014360
The supplier shall provide asessment on the risks derived from any openings or cavities formed by vehicle structures that interfere with the sensors field of view within 180 degrees, delivering a document with final statement and suggested actions.
Comment00357243
Openings or cavities formed by surrounding surfaces could create conditions for multiple reflections resulting in an extended and undesired return path of ultrasonic waves. Sensor integration shall aim to eliminate known factors contributing to false detection caused by integration of sensors in such areas.
Vicinity of hot air sources

Vicinity of hot air sources
Description

chunks.content_text:
Vicinity of hot air sources
Description
The purpose of this requirement is to eliminate known factors contributing to false detection caused by refraction. Refraction is a phenomenon taking place when a wave passes from one medium to another, resulting in a change of its direction. It also applies to ultrasonic waves traveling across a boundary created by cold and hot air areas. NOTE: General guidelines contained herein help to minimize the risk of unwanted reflections, but are not exhaustive due to the nature of the phenomenon. Additional tests on representative vehicles are recommended.
Rear exhaust pipe
Description
Reflections from exhaust gases are likely to happen if they accumulate in the field of view of the sensors. Contributing factors are windless weather, vehicle not moving or slow backward driving.
Minimum distance of the sensor
Sensor direction relative to exhaust pipe
-
Front grille and air intakes
Description
Hot air pushed out of the engine compartment through the front grilles or air intakes produces hot air accumulation in the bumper vicinity. This may lead to unwanted reflections of ultrasonic waves and change their propagation path. This is particularly important if the correct system integration was achieved by use of near field filters or similar feature, which minimizes the influence of the vehicle’s own geometry on the echo received by the sensors.
Positioning in heat sources vicinity
The ultrasonic sensor integration shall ensure that the sensor is placed in a volume where the air temperature is kept below 95ºC while in operation.
Comment00357013

Positioning in heat sources vicinity
The ultrasonic sensor integration shall ensure that the sensor is placed in a volume where the air temperature is kept below 95ºC while in operation.
Comment00357013
Impact of hot air should be minimized. Alternative sensor positions or other means of keeping them away from heat sources should be considered.
Vehicle Zones
Comment00321943
The USS sensor can be considered under the following package zone (as defined in STJLR.00.5164):
Mechanical design
Sensor holder
Water management
Water drainage
Water drainage is necessary to ensure proper operation of sensors. Residual water has a tendency to flow upward in narrow gaps due to capillary action. This may cause unwanted coupling between the sensor housing and its membrane. When water residues freeze and expand, additional pressure on the sensor housing may be generated resulting in sensor deactivation or false detections.
Sensor integration with holder
The holder design and sensor integration shall guarantee no gap condition between the sensor housing and the DCR in the range of expected tolerances.
Drainage hole location
The sensor holder shall comprise an aperture, which prevents water accumulation and ensures it can freely drain away from DCR area.
Comment00361985
The drainage aperture shall be as close as possible to the decopling ring.
This location is convenient to evacuate water that may accumulate in the DCR vicinity after situations like a pressure wash.
Drainage hole

chunks.content_text:
Comment00361985
The drainage aperture shall be as close as possible to the decopling ring.
This location is convenient to evacuate water that may accumulate in the DCR vicinity after situations like a pressure wash.
Drainage hole
The geometry of the drainage hole shall create a cut perpendicular to the ground plane of the vehicle and large enough to fully fit a square with a side of: [shall] minimum 4 mm (including tolerances) [Desirable] 5 mm (including tolerances)
Drainage hole clearance
The area under the drainage hole shall provide a clearance of: minimum 5 mm Required due to possible water accumulation at the sensor (despite the presence of drainage hole), caused by barriers in the form of other attachment parts. The above requirements shall be met on an assembled vehicle. Any technological limitations compromising location of drainage hole and its desired geometry for a given design concept, shall be reported by the sensor holder manufacturer followed by the sensor supplier and ADAS team assessment.
Drainage hole geometry
[RQ_413] In order to facilitate undisturbed water flow, the acceptable size of burrs around the edge of the drainage hole shall measure: less than 0.2 mm
Poka-yoke features
All sensor holders shall comprise poka-yoke features or similar measures to ensure that sensor and sensor holders cannot be mis-fitted.
Sensor holder Materials
Description
This section contains materials requirements for the sensor holder and installation area and explains related limitations.
Material recommendations
The mechanical interface of the sensor to the bumper shall be made of PP material.

Sensor holder Materials
Description
This section contains materials requirements for the sensor holder and installation area and explains related limitations.
Material recommendations
The mechanical interface of the sensor to the bumper shall be made of PP material.
NOTE: The use of any other material is not allowed without previous acceptance from the supplier.
Comment00357266
According to lessons learnt with previous USS systems, the use of the following materials in the mechanical interface of the sensor shouldn't affect the sensor performance.
Comment00357258
Following materials are not recommended to use:
Hard materials or non-elastomeric modified thermoplastics such as pure amorphous plastics (like PC or PC-blends) and metallic components are not recommended for use due to their unfavourable acoustical properties
Required material properties
Selected material should have the following properties:
Requirement00874368
The USS holder shall be attached to the bumper in the position and orientation defined in the bumper CAD design.
Process related
Description
This section contains mechanical design requirements related to manufacturing and assembly processes.
Process related
Mechanical load onto the sensor housing shall be less than or equal to 75N after completion of the assembly process.
Mechanical load on sensor membrane
No mechanical load shall be present on the sensor membranes during and after assembly process (in particular twisting or lateral force)
No damage to decoupling ring
The sensor fitment shall avoid causing any damage to the DCR (for example by burrs or sharp edges).

Description
This section contains mechanical design requirements related to manufacturing and assembly processes.
Process related

chunks.content_text:
Mechanical load on sensor membrane
No mechanical load shall be present on the sensor membranes during and after assembly process (in particular twisting or lateral force)
No damage to decoupling ring
The sensor fitment shall avoid causing any damage to the DCR (for example by burrs or sharp edges).
NOTE: fitment comprises the sensor holder, the bumper and whatever means used to attach the holder to the bumper.
Durability
Sensor holder
Sensor Retention Force
The sensor and relevant mechanical interfaces shall remain securely held within the holder when a force of 70 N < F1 < 75 N is applied for 2 seconds and 3 times as per TPJLR 18.201
Sensor disengagement force
The sensor holder and relevant mechanical interfaces shall ensure that the sensor disengages from the holder if the axial push force is greater or equal than 75 N applied on the sensor membrane face as per TPJLR 18.201
Sensor unlatching force
The sensor and relevant mechanical interfaces shall remain securely held within the holder when a pulling force on its harness of 35 N < F2 < 45 N is applied for 2 seconds and 3 times as per TPJLR 18.201
Number of insertion cycles
The sensor holder shall withstand a minimum of 5 sensor insertion and removal cycles without being damaged, losing its mechanical properties or causing damage to the sensor.
Fastening
Holder detachment force
[RQ_520] The chosen fastening method shall ensure that the sensor holder is securely attached to the installation surface upto a detaching force of greater than or equal to 150 N.
Painting Requirements
Membrane Coating

Membrane Coating
[RQ_530] The sensor membrane coating shall meet the requirements for exterior painted parts referred in STJLR.51.5241.
This requirement applies to standard coatings offered or developed by the sensor supplier or integrator (powder coating, body colour paints) and those provided by any other paint shop chosen.

There are two situations where we need the supplier to deliver unpainted sensors that will be painted under the control of JLR,
under both situations the paint process shall comply with the following requirements.

chunks.content_text:
Requirement01017202
The ultrasonic sensor integration shall be done according to the Supplier Integration Guidelines.
NOTE: Any deviation from the supplier integration guidelines for USS positioning shall get the acceptance from the USS supplier.
USS positioning deviations from mounting guidelines
In case of any deviation of the final sensor positioning with respect to the supplier mounting guidelines, the supplier shall review the deviation and provide an evaluation report of the risks derived.
NOTE: final sensor position includes the tolerances.
Comment00357758
The integration guidelines provided by supplier will include a graph reflecting the allowed pitch angles for the sensor as a function of the sensor height, this is a useful tool that functional package will use to guide the discussions with the design team, however the design constraints and manufacturing tolerances will likely force the sensor to deviate under some situations from the recomended positioning. The final assessment from the supplier as technical expert is required to evaluate the possible risks of those deviations and raise the required corrective actions.
Height and beta angle based positioning
The sensor's nominal position across the whole suspension height range shall be within the green zone of the height vs beta angle graph shared by the supplier as part of the integration guidelines.
Requirement01017223
The sensor's final position across the whole suspension height range considering the manufacturing tolerances shall be within the green and yellow zones of the height vs beta angle graph shared by the supplier as part of the integration guidelines.
Requirement01017224

Requirement01017223
The sensor's final position across the whole suspension height range considering the manufacturing tolerances shall be within the green and yellow zones of the height vs beta angle graph shared by the supplier as part of the integration guidelines.
Requirement01017224
Any deviation that causes the sensor's final position to be in a red zone of the height vs beta angle graph shall be agreed with and accepted by the supplier.
Comment00358578
positive Beta angles will provide better detection performance in presence of ground clutter than negative beta angles,
Positive beta angles will be preferred over negative beta angles,
in terms of the graph, it is preferred to package the sensors in the left side of the green zone.
Height and beta angle assessment
The supplier shall review the relation between the final height and final beta angle and evaluate the risk derived, providing a written statement of acceptance.
NOTE: final height and final beta angle include the tolerances
USS positioning around license plate
The minimum distance of the USS(considering centre of USS membrane) particularly at position S9/S10 , S3/S4 shall be 40 mm and 60 mm from the vertical and horizontal sides of license plate respectively as shown in the figure below.
Requirement01053946
For any sensor located at 40 mm and 60 mm from the vertical and horizontal sides of license plate respectively (measured from the centre of USS membrane), the distance in the X direction from the sensor membrane to the furthest point of the license plate shall be ≤ 20 mm.
